issues.issue: First edition printed Chapter LXXXVII after duplicated LXXXV; stable sequential source alias LXXXVIII.
Body opens PDF491 below separate Eleventh House heading, and concludes PDF492 before PDF493 next chapter.
Eleventh House covers friends, hoped-for objects and rulers' riches, which are not interchangeable endpoints.
Source provides generic rule examples, not dated named questions with independently documented human outcomes.
Historical house-lord placements, receptions and light translations are not independently calculated or calibrated.
The basic favourable variants are disjunctive: aspect, reception, translation, first lord in eleventh, eleventh lord in first.
The Moon fallback negative requires lack of other good testimonies and lack of qualification to eleventh lord.
Moon related to eleventh is not a standalone unconditional promise of receiving every hoped-for object.
Requests to a Prince, noble, lord or master are examples of historical patronage, not always direct employment.
Applying lord of eleventh to first versus first to eleventh are different directed configurations.
Trine/sextile versus square/opposition change ease and speed, not simply success versus failure.
Source expressly says square/opposition may still lead to attainment even when reception occurs.
Angular eleventh ruler with reception is a separate strong conclusion, not interchangeable with any angular planet.
Moon's disposition receiver in common, movable or fixed signs yields **part**, **mere possibility/very little**, or **complete** results respectively.
Traditional terms common and movable are source-specific categories; do not silently collapse common into cardinal signs.
An unfortunate Moon receiver can mean damage after obtaining the hoped-for thing; damage is a second event distinct from failure to acquire.
Moon receiver received and lord ascendant received are different favourable routes.
The final prediction is expressly restricted by Lilly to **feasible and possible** things.
Following printed LXXXVIII, editorial LXXXIX 'Of agreeing of Friends' starts PDF493, outside this chapter.
No independent event registry, contemporaneous prediction deposit, baseline comparison, or out-of-sample validation is included.
No runtime model weights/empirical predictions can be promoted from historical source documentation.
